The suspect should be found not guilty if the jury believes his account, because a statute that forbids force to resist a known arrest still leaves the privilege to use reasonable force against an officer’s excessive force, and one punch to stop an unprovoked nightstick beating falls within that privilege. He should be found guilty if the jury believes the officer, because that account has him striking first to resist the arrest. Either result holds whether the arrest itself was lawful or unlawful.

CONFIDENCE: 82
